title: I built a vaporwave mallsoft FPS with my own model agnostic AI tool. Here's the weapons trailer, all in-engine
author: lanepin
selftext:
Vaporware 94 is a first-person shooter set in an endless 1994 mall. It's built in Godot, and I wrote it with Privateer. A private AI platform I built. Some of the models, sprites and art were made with with it. Everything in the trailer is real in-engine footage, not generated video.

Five weapons, three tiers each, and every tier swaps the model and changes the shot: GUI Glock, Trance Fade, Chroma Cannon, 16-BITE, Mallrun Blade.

I'm streaming the demo later today. More at [vaporware94.com](http://vaporware94.com)

Epic page: [https://store.epicgames.com/p/vaporware-94-7d9e21](https://store.epicgames.com/p/vaporware-94-7d9e21)

comments.author: SryNot
comments.body:
I respect everyone who builds their own stuff, but I think you are shooting yourself in the foot using your own model agnostic AI tool. Here's why:

1. You do not get the subsidized usage of frontier models. If you use a Claude Code or Gemini subscription directly, they will give you 20-40x more usage compared to equivalent direct API usage. So you pay $200 and get $10k in equivalent API usage per month. You really want to be using Claude Code, ChatGPT, or Gemini Neon right now because they are way better than any other option at game dev especially.  
2. Models work better in their own harnesses, end of story. Claude works best in Claude Code because that's where the training data comes from. 

If you are doing it for fun and learning, go for it. But it will be much easier to finish your game and make it high quality using the subscriptions directly. If you want a consistent workflow, consider t3code which allows using any subscription with one coding tool easily

replies.author: lanepin
replies.body: I built Privateer in regards to privacy. Anthropic and Google, almost everything they do with AI uses your data and stores it in plain text on their servers. Who knows what they'll use it for down the line, especially as AI advances. ALSO I believe open source models like will become more capable and affordable to keep up with these closed companies trying to maintain a moat by locking users into their eco system.

replies.author: lanepin
replies.body:
Privateer connects to various ai providers running inference on either zero data retention policies (which have been known to be vulnerable) and those running models on trusted execution environments where your prompts are encrypted on your client and sent to a secure compute enclave that providers have no ability to view.

I personally like knowing that certain things, work, ideas and questions can stay private to me and i figured that would be a value prop for others so that's why i built it. 🤷‍♂️

replies.author: lanepin
replies.body:
I used Privateer, my own harness built aroud surfacing privacy ai providers. It's model agnostic, connecting to various providers to provide every asset generation required to make a game, 3d models, sfx, voices, sprites, images etc... When i started this project i was mostly using glm 5.3 flash/glm 5.3 and opus 5 at the time.

I did a 30 day livestream of the first days of development. Here's day 1: [https://www.youtube.com/live/oTTqHNUoyfE?si=tp-j6rGNmy5hbZcu](https://www.youtube.com/live/oTTqHNUoyfE?si=tp-j6rGNmy5hbZcu)
